title: Pelorus Healthcare — on‑prem handoff notes
content:
Meeting: Pelorus HC on‑prem kickoff / handoff
Date: 2025-11-19
Attendees: Pelorus: Dr. Asha Banerjee (CTO), Marco Ruiz (Infra), Priya Nair (Security) — Redwood: Elena Rossi (SE lead), Samir Gupta (infra), Maya Chen (privacy)

Context / goal:
- Pelorus runs clinical decision support in hospitals; cannot send PHI to public clouds. They want Redwood Private deployed into their VMware cluster (air‑gapped option under evaluation). Primary objective is: run inference on open LLMs for summarization and triage with strict auditability and <150ms median token latency target for 512‑token tails.

Quick summary of asks from call:
- Private control plane (customer managed) with on‑prem inference nodes behind hospital firewall.
- KMS integration: must support AWS CloudHSM via PKCS#11 bridge (they use a local HSM appliance).
- FIPS/algo list: AES‑GCM for disk/transport, avoid legacy ciphers.
- Audit logs must contain tokenized prompt/response hashes, not raw PHI; Pelorus will provide hashing policy.
- Network: no outbound traffic except to Redwood control plane endpoints on specified allowlist or optionally entirely offline with manual model packaging.
- Model lineage & pinned versions for clinical validation; ability to freeze model hashes and config for audits.

Current infra notes (from Marco):
- VMware ESXi 7.0 on two racks, access to 4x A40 GPUs via passthrough; internal k8s (Rancher) 1.27 in staging.
- Internal artifact store (Artifactory) and S3‑compatible object store (MinIO) accessible on private network.
- On‑prem NTP and LDAP/AD for user mapping.

Technical constraints / gotchas identified:
1) GPU compatibility: A40 supports mixed precision well but current kernel on their hosts uses older Nvidia driver (470.x). Need driver >=510 for Triton‑adjacent optimizations. Action: Samir to draft driver upgrade checklist and risk rollback plan.
2) Air‑gapped model packaging: They prefer zero outbound. We must provide a signed package workflow (model artifacts + runtime) and a checksum manifest. Offline package flow isn't fully hardened in current release; expect ~2 week eng work for full signed package UX.
3) HSM integration: PKCS#11 bridge tested only with SoftHSM in our lab. Real hardware could require vendor middleware; schedule vendor handshake.
4) Latency target: 150ms median for 512 tokens is aggressive on A40 with current quantized llama‑style models unless continuous batching is disabled and KV cache pinned per user. Need to set batching config per route and ensure SLOs.
5) Audit logging / PHI: Pelorus will not accept raw token logs. We need to pipeline log hashing on the host before transport to control plane. That requires a local hashing service or a client‑side plugin.

Security / compliance notes:
- Data residency: all PHI must remain inside hospital network unless explicitly allowed for dev telemetry (they will not allow telemetry initially).
- RBAC: map AD groups to Redwood roles; want read‑only analytics for compliance auditors.
- Retention policy: transcripts hashed and retained for 7 years per their legal. Must provide deletion hooks.

Model & runtime decisions discussed:
- Start with open LLaMA‑derived 13B quantized (int8) for triage; later evaluate 33B for complex summarization.
- Recommend Redwood Optimize profile: aggressive KV caching + prefix caching enabled for triage flows.
- Quantization: use S4/QLoRa pipelines for accuracy checks; Pelorus legal requires a model quality gate before production.

Observability & rollouts:
- They need per‑route latency and per‑token cost breakdowns, but dashboards will be hosted locally on the private console.
- Canaries: prefer traffic shadowing first, then 1% canary for doctors in staging site.

Open questions to resolve with Pelorus:
- Do they accept hashed token counts for billing/usage metering or insist on exact raw token counts? (billing/privacy tradeoff)
- HSM vendor/model + middleware version (Marco to provide exact model numbers).
- Acceptance criteria for model quality gate (exact eval prompts + pass thresholds).
- How strict is their no‑outbound policy for package signing key rotation?

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Samir: driver compatibility matrix + upgrade rollback plan draft — due 2025-11-26.
- Elena: offline model packaging requirements doc (technical checklist + manifest schema) — draft by 2025-11-28.
- Maya: PHI hashing design options (client‑side vs host‑side) and implications for audit logs — due 2025-11-25.
- Marco (Pelorus): send HSM appliance model & firmware, and list of internal hostnames for allowlist — by 2025-11-24.
- Sync: schedule deep technical workshop (2 hours) with Pelorus infra + security + Redwood infra/eng — target week of 2025-12-01. Elena to propose times.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: driver upgrade causes node instability. Mitigation: test on 2 spare hosts first, snapshot VMs, staged upgrade sequence.
- Risk: air‑gap signing UX delay. Mitigation: provide manual guidance and temporary semi‑offline mode (control plane minimal egress) as interim.
- Risk: HSM incompatibility. Mitigation: vendor vendor‑to‑vendor proxy or fallback to software keystore with additional auditing for initial pilot.

Notes to self / internal items:
- Loop in release‑engineering for offline package signing requirements (ticket GH-PR-3412 linked).
- Prepare a short one‑pager for Pelorus legal on what we can and cannot guarantee re: PHI hashing and model outputs.
- Estimate rough costs for Dedicated vs Private baseline for their scale (4 GPUs + 2 spares) and include OpEx for signed package support.

TL;DR: Pelorus wants a fully private, audit‑worthy inference stack with no outbound PHI. Major pieces to solve in short term: driver upgrade, offline model packaging, HSM integration, and PHI‑safe logging. Next workshop to finalize packaging/KMS path and acceptance criteria for model quality gate.

Action items snapshot (editable):
- [ ] Samir — driver matrix + rollback plan — 2025-11-26
- [ ] Elena — offline packaging spec — 2025-11-28
- [ ] Maya — PHI hashing design + pros/cons — 2025-11-25
- [ ] Marco (Pelorus) — HSM details + host allowlist — 2025-11-24
- [ ] Elena + Marco — schedule technical workshop week of 2025-12-01

End of notes.
